rounds.text: Savy Infra and Logistics Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted P/E of just 5.84x while demonstrating explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion, with 3-year compounded sales growth reaching 369% and compounded profit growth hitting 398% [E1, E8, E10]. The business generates elite returns on capital, backed by a stellar ROCE of 42.8% and a 3-year median ROE of 53%, vastly outperforming sector medians [E6, E13, E49]. Furthermore, intrinsic value models indicate a massive margin of safety, and the reverse DCF reveals that the current market price incorrectly prices in a negative 9.4% earnings contraction against an actual base case of 18.0% growth [E30, E31, E32]. Profit and sales continue to rise sequentially on a multi-year uptrend, showing that the company is starting to outperform expectations as recent profit growth outpaces 1-year price performance by 89% [E34, E40, E41, E42, E43]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -51 Cr and institutional shareholding has seen outflows [E20, E27, E28, E29].

Despite reported profit growth, Savy Infra and Logistics Ltd suffers from a severe cash flow disconnect, posting a negative cash conversion of -1.21x with operating cash flow plunging to Rs -51 Cr and free cash flow sinking to Rs -57 Cr in Mar 2026 [E19, E20, E21]. This liquidity drain is compounded by rising borrowings, which increased to Rs 52 Cr alongside a worsening working capital cycle where working capital days expanded from 58.5 days to 86.9 days [E24, E38]. Institutional confidence is actively eroding through negative money flow and visible outflows, with foreign institutional holdings dropping to 0.40% and domestic institutional holdings falling to 0.82% [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield despite its reported profits, and operating margins remain inconsistent while sitting lower over a three-year horizon [E4, E16, E17, E37]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical return metrics including a 42.8% ROCE and a 3-year median ROE of 53%, alongside rapid top-line and bottom-line compounding [E6, E8, E10, E14].

Conceded: operating cash flow sits at Rs -51 Cr and free cash flow at Rs -57 Cr in Mar 2026 [E20, E21], and borrowings rose to Rs 52 Cr alongside higher working capital days [E24, E38]. However, this near-term liquidity tightness is vastly overstated as a structural flaw when evaluated against the company's elite capital efficiency, demonstrated by a 42.8% ROCE and a 3-year median ROE of 53% [E6, E14]. Conceded: institutional holdings have contracted and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E27, E28], but institutional outflows merely present a mispriced entry point given that profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 89%, signaling that the market is only just beginning to catch up to fundamental outperformance [E34]. Furthermore, the bear's fixation on margin inconsistency ignores a multi-year sales uptrend and 3-year compounded profit growth of 398% [E10, E42], proving that explosive top- and bottom-line scaling dwarfs minor operating margin fluctuations.

Conceded: multi-year profit growth stands at 398% [E10]. However, dismissing severe cash burn as mere near-term tightness ignores that operating cash flow plunged to Rs -51 Cr and free cash flow to Rs -57 Cr in Mar 2026, dragging cash conversion down to -1.21x [E19, E20, E21]. The bull claims institutional outflows offer a mispriced entry point, yet foreign and domestic institutions have actively reduced their stakes from 3.21% to 0.40% and 2.26% to 0.82% respectively, generating negative institutional money flow [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, pointing to elite capital efficiency rings hollow when working capital days have worsened from 58.5 days to 86.9 days alongside rising borrowings of Rs 52 Cr [E24, E38]. Conceded: sales and profits show strong historical uptrends [E42, E43], but this growth has failed to translate into shareholder returns as evidenced by a 0.00% dividend yield and a 13% share price decline over the past year [E4, E12]. Finally, the claim that explosive scaling dwarfs operating margin fluctuations is undermined by inconsistent yearly and quarterly margins coupled with a declining operating margin trend [E16, E17, E18].
